To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DPM is not suitable for use with the LHC experiments, because of the high overheads of the POSIX interface.

1) the DPM client is not able to saturate the network link to the DPM server; 2) this is due to an inability of the DPM client to issue multiple concurrent requests to the DPM service, which is limited to one at any time; 3) we have implemented a new client library that is able to saturate a 1 Gbps network link, and we are currently working on an optimised client library that will saturate a 10 G
DPM can provide good read/write throughput, but the latency of the DPM interface is high and is the dominant factor for small files.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How does the DPM file system perform when used to store and retrieve files from a Grid enabled storage element? (2) How can the performance be optimised to meet the requirements of the WLCG?
the performance of DPM SEs when accessed via the Grid.
the performance of the DPM POSIX-like client and how to optimise it to provide the best possible performance for the WLCG.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current performance of POSIX-like read and write access to the Grid storage elements is not satisfactory.
, in general, the performance of POSIX access to DPM files is poor.
the current version of the DPM software is not suitable for the access patterns envisaged for Tier2s in the WLCG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DPM is a viable solution for Tier-2 storage, provided that the storage is optimised for the expected usage pattern.
the performance of the DPM POSIX interface is adequate for the majority of use cases.
we can achieve POSIX-like access with reasonable performance to files stored in DPM SEs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of DPM is not as poor as has been previously reported, but that there are significant differences between the performance of different versions of DPM.
the DPM storage manager is able to provide POSIX-like access with performance similar to native access to a local file system.
, in general, the use of DPM as a POSIX-like file server is sub-optimal for the WLCG.
